passage.text: This article describes the diagnostic process in psychotherapy when it is based on aesthetic evaluation. Unlike the classical diagnostic process, which compares a clinician's observations with a diagnostic system such as DSM or ICD, aesthetic evaluation is pre-reflexive, embodied, and preverbal. The article uses a Gestalt Therapy theoretical framework to introduce the concept of an aesthetic diagnostic process. During this process, clinicians use their own here-and-now presence, which contributes to the co-creation of a shared relational field within the therapeutic session. The article also introduces a specific procedure for carrying out aesthetic evaluation. Clinical work with depressed clients is then presented in order to illustrate this perspective.

source.title: Article Aesthetic Diagnosis in Gestalt Therapy

taps.correct: Aesthetic evaluation offers an alternative diagnostic approach based on immediate embodied perception rather than comparing observations to diagnostic manuals.
wrong: Classical diagnostic systems like DSM are replaced entirely by aesthetic evaluation.
Gestalt Therapy is superior to all other psychotherapeutic approaches.
taps.explain: The excerpt contrasts two approaches but doesn't eliminate classical diagnosis.

taps.explain: The procedure is for carrying out aesthetic evaluation, not other concepts.
